disclaimer: Illustrative training content for the hackathon demonstration; not a validated mechanical procedure.

task.title: Shaft and Bearing Inspection
task.description: Illustrative inspection training for an unpowered shaft-and-bearing bench assembly.

knowledge_units.action: Rotate the shaft slowly by hand through one full turn
knowledge_units.cue: Illustrative: a visible wobble at the shaft end during rotation
knowledge_units.interpretation: Illustrative: possible misalignment between the shaft and the bearing
knowledge_units.decision: Illustrative: stop and check bearing seating before continuing the inspection

knowledge_units.action: Check that the base mounting fasteners are present

evidence_items.content: Illustrative description of a demonstration segment: the expert inspects the bearing housing.
Illustrative example: if the shaft end wobbles while turning it by hand, I stop and check how the bearing is seated before going further.
Illustrative description of a demonstration segment: the expert checks the base mounting fasteners.

example_expert_responses.answer: Illustrative example: I look at the housing first for grease leaking at the seal or discoloration. Leaking grease suggests the seal or bearing may be damaged, so I do not rotate the shaft until a supervisor has checked it.

fields.cue: Illustrative: grease leaking at the housing seal or discoloration on the housing
fields.interpretation: Illustrative: possible seal or bearing damage
fields.decision: Illustrative: do not rotate the shaft; escalate to a supervisor before continuing

baseline_release.approval_note: Illustrative baseline release seeded for demonstration.

questions.prompt: Why should the inspection and verification checks be recorded before a release decision?

options.label: The model looks complete, so no record is needed.
options.feedback: A rendered view is insufficient evidence for a release decision.

options.label: The decision should be supported by the observations and authored check results.
options.feedback: The recorded checks make the decision traceable; the rendering alone cannot validate real fit.

options.label: Recording is useful only after a problem occurs.
options.feedback: Record checks before deciding so the reasoning remains traceable.

questions.prompt: A later check raises an unresolved concern about alignment. What should happen next?

options.label: Release the assembly because the earlier animation succeeded.
options.feedback: An animation does not resolve the later concern.

options.label: Stop release and ask for review of the unresolved evidence.
options.feedback: Preserve the unresolved observation and seek review before release.

options.label: Ignore the concern if the assembly looks centered.
options.feedback: Visual confidence cannot resolve missing approved evidence.

questions.prompt: What can this illustrative exercise establish about a real bearing assembly?

options.label: It certifies the assembly is safe for service.
options.feedback: This exercise does not certify mechanical safety or real-world readiness.

options.label: It proves the real assembly meets required tolerances.
options.feedback: The scripted exercise does not calculate or verify physical tolerances.

options.label: It records training choices; supervised practical assessment is still needed.
options.feedback: The report describes training decisions and their rationale. Practical assessment remains necessary.
